title: Deterministic Markov Text Generator
prompt:
Implement `transition_counts(corpus)` and `generate_text(corpus, start, steps)`. Tokenize the corpus with the regex `[a-z]+(?:'[a-z]+)*` after lowercasing; thus "It's" becomes "it's" and differs from "its". Punctuation and digits separate tokens. Count each adjacent token pair over the entire corpus, including across punctuation. Return a dict mapping words with outgoing edges to dicts of next-word counts.

Generation normalizes start with the same tokenizer; start is guaranteed to contain exactly one token and steps is a nonnegative integer. Return a space-joined string starting with that token, followed by at most steps transitions. Choose the most frequent next word, breaking ties lexicographically. Stop at a word with no outgoing edge, including an unseen start or empty corpus. Do not sample randomly.

Reconstruction assumptions: tokenization, punctuation boundary behavior, and lexical tie-breaking were unspecified in the source and are explicitly fixed here. Discuss how a sampled Markov model would differ.

example.reasoning: b and c tie after a; b is lexically first and terminal.
